newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end stable on returning payment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end stable on returning payment.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed stable on Wednesday with market liquidity fuelled by the return of T$30 billion government bond principle and interest payments to the banking system, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended unchanged at 7.274 percent -- far outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but still below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper rose to 7.25-7.50 percent against 7.25-7.35.
Dealers said the rates did not have room to fall because excess funds continued to stream out of the banking system into the stock market.
The local bourse suffered heavy profit-taking on Wednesday following a recent bull charge, tumbling 1.77 percent to close at 9,381.06. But turnover remained heavy at T$189 billion.
The central bank issued T$8 billion negotiable certificates of deposit to mop up liquidity.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.9775 percent against 5.9665-9675.
